text:
Anna: :warning: Getting escalations from multiple customers (ACME, BetaCorp) — hosted inference endpoints returning 502/504 and client timeouts starting ~2024-04-22 09:15 UTC. Opening thread here for triage and repro notes.
Mike: Oncall me. Can you paste an example request/response and any correlation IDs?
Anna: Example curl from support repro:```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.prod/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"rwd-xl-1","input":"hello"}'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout` or occasionally `502 Bad Gateway`. Correlation header: `x-rwd-cid: rwd-5n2b-abc123`
Sam: I'm seeing the same CID in edge logs, requests are hitting the gateway then timing out waiting for backend pool. Backend traces show long queue times on the gpu-infer-pool in eu-west.
Julia: Customer notes: bulk/streaming jobs spiking at 09:10–09:20 UTC, some clients report sudden retry storms. Billing auth checks look fine. No KMS errors.
ops-bot: deploy notification: `deploy/rwd-inference-gateway` started at 2024-04-22T08:58:32Z by ci/cd.
Mike: Good to know. Hypothesis: deployment changed concurrency or timeouts on gateway or autoscaler didn't scale fast enough. Checking gateway config and autoscaler events.
Sam: Adding quick mitigations: 1) increase gateway upstream timeout to 70s, 2) temporarily enable fallback routing to smaller model variant (rwd-medium-1) for read-heavy routes, 3) bump autoscaler min replicas for gpu-infer-pool. Doing 1 and 3 now.
Anna: Noted — pinged support to tell impacted customers we're investigating and to disable aggressive client retries for 15m.
Mike: I queried autoscaler events: scale-up requests queued, but cloud provider rate-limited new instance creation for ~4m due to burst limits. That's why scaling lagged.
Sam: Workaround applied: enabled fallback routing to dedicated warm standby nodes (reserved pool) for critical customers — rolling config now.
Julia: Confirming BetaCorp latency dropped after fallback enabled. ACME still seeing some 502s but volume reduced.
Mike: Root cause draft: (a) sudden client retry spike increased QPS, (b) autoscaler throttled by provider burst limits causing delay in capacity, (c) gateway upstream timeout conservative and didn't fallback quickly.
Anna: Repro steps we've captured so far: 1) Send burst of parallel requests (~200 qps sustained for 2m) targeting /v1/generate with streaming flag on, 2) watch gateway logs for `upstream timed out` and backend queue_ms > 2000, 3) observe provider api returning rate limit errors for instance create.
Sam: Immediate action items (assigned):
- Mike: create short-term runbook to detect provider rate-limits and preemptively raise capacity (ETA 2h)
- Sam: add automatic fallback policy to route to warm standby when queue_ms > 1000 (ETA 1h)
- Julia: customer comms template for impacted accounts + offer mitigation credits (ETA 30m)
- Anna: collect sample traces & example request IDs for postmortem (ETA EOD)
Mike: Long-term action ideas: increase autoscaler burst quota with provider, make a circuit-breaker on gateway that triggers fallback earlier, catalog per-tenant retry patterns to throttle noisy clients.
Anna: Putting a short postmortem/warroom follow-up meeting at 14:00 UTC today to agree on RCA and next steps.
Sam: Quick note — please add an item to run a chaos test: simulate instance creation throttling and verify fallback behavior.
Julia: :white_check_mark: I'll draft comms and ping legal for credits wording.
ops-bot: incident updated: severity set to S2 by Mike.
Anna: Thanks all — will update thread as we get more telemetry.
